text:
sam: heads up — after yesterday's attention-kernel swap on Mixtral-10B we see a 9-12% latency win but perf tests show a quality regression on long-context evals (>=2048).

anna: saw this too, narrowed it to the fused_attention_v2 kernel + rope scaling tweak. small prompt shift causes response truncation / odd repeats.

derrick: perf numbers?

sam: profiler output (sample):
```
model: mixtral-10b
kernel: fused_attention_v2
median_latency: 78ms -> 68ms (-13%)
p50/p95: 64/140 -> 56/125
eval: long_context_pass@2048 dropped 0.91 -> 0.78
```

sam: also noticed KV cache hit-rate dips when streaming partial outputs — seems cache keys differ after kernel swap (different padding/pack order).

lee: interesting — could be batch packing heuristics interacting with kernel input layout. We changed packing to micro-batch-first to feed fused kernel; kv index depends on (seq_len, padding_mask) ordering.

anna: on Mistral we saw similar but smaller effects. Qwen configs unaffected so far — different head/kv dims.

derrick: any config diff we can revert quickly?

sam: two options: rollback kernel to fused_attention_v1 OR keep kernel and disable the new rope_scaling dynamic mode for mixtral models.

ci-bot: deploy 2026-03-22T09:14:12Z: canary rollout of fused_attention_v2 to 25% (mixtral-10b)

sam: canary triggered the eval regression alarms (e2e-evals long-context). It's noisy but reproducible across 10 seeds.

lee: quick experiment idea: preserve kernel but change batching: force `preserve_batch_order=true` and `max_batch_tokens=2048` to keep layout stable. If hit-rate recovers, it's packing-related.

anna: I'll run that locally against the regression prompt set.

(30m later)

anna: results: with preserved order hit-rate back to baseline and eval pass@2048 recovered to 0.90. Latency slightly worse than canary but still net win vs v1.

sam: great. so root cause is interaction of batching heuristics + kernel input layout + rope scaling. rope scaling exposed sensitivity to token positions when packing changed.

derrick: what's the plan? revert config or patch runtime to compute canonical KV keys independent of packing?

lee: patch idea: canonicalize kv index using global_pos instead of local packed index. Prototype:
```
kv_key = (model_id, layer, head, global_pos_start, token_count)
```
should be stable regardless of packing.

sam: nice. short-term: roll back canary to v1 to stop traffic hit, then deploy two-step: batching change + canonical KV in runtime + small rope scaling tweak.

perf-bot: alert: canary rollback initiated by sam at 2026-03-22T09:52:03Z

anna: I'll own the canonical KV prototype and run full eval sweep (mixtral/mistral/llama) — target: PR + bench in 24h.

lee: I'll prepare a safer canary plan: 5% -> 25% with eval gate and KV hit-rate monitor.

derrick: document decision: do not change quantization flags during kernel work without eval sweep. last time a quant toggle + kernel swap caused subtle output shifts.

sam: agreed. also add automated eval for rope-sensitivity (long context cohesion) to CI.

anna: filing follow-ups: #1 PR for canonical KV proto, #2 batching repro test, #3 CI eval job for rope scaling.

(+: :thumbsup: from lee, derrick)
